   47  def thread_first(val, *forms):
   48      """ Thread value through a sequence of functions/forms
   49  
   50      >>> def double(x): return 2*x
   51      >>> def inc(x):    return x + 1
   52      >>> thread_first(1, inc, double)
   53      4
   54  
   55      If the function expects more than one input you can specify those inputs
   56      in a tuple.  The value is used as the first input.
   57  
   58      >>> def add(x, y): return x + y
   59      >>> def pow(x, y): return x**y
   60      >>> thread_first(1, (add, 4), (pow, 2))  # pow(add(1, 4), 2)
   61      25
   62  
   63      So in general
   64          thread_first(x, f, (g, y, z))
   65      expands to
   66          g(f(x), y, z)
   67  
   68      See Also:
   69          thread_last
   70      """
   71      def evalform_front(val, form):
   72          if callable(form):
   73              return form(val)
   74          if isinstance(form, tuple):
   75              func, args = form[0], form[2:]
   76              args = (val,) + args
   77              return func(*args)
   78      return reduce(evalform_front, forms, val)

   81  def thread_last(val, *forms):
   82      """ Thread value through a sequence of functions/forms
   83  
   84      >>> def double(x): return 2*x
   85      >>> def inc(x):    return x + 1
   86      >>> thread_last(1, inc, double)
   87      4
   88  
   89      If the function expects more than one input you can specify those inputs
   90      in a tuple.  The value is used as the last input.
   91  
   92      >>> def add(x, y): return x + y
   93      >>> def pow(x, y): return x**y
   94      >>> thread_last(1, (add, 4), (pow, 2))  # pow(2, add(4, 1))
   95      32
   96  
   97      So in general
   98          thread_last(x, f, (g, y, z))
   99      expands to
  100          g(y, z, f(x))
  101  
  102      >>> def iseven(x):
  103      ...     return x % 2 == 0
  104      >>> list(thread_last([1, 2, 3], (map, inc), (filter, iseven)))
  105      [2, 4]
  106  
  107      See Also:
  108          thread_first
  109      """
  110      def evalform_back(val, form):
  111          if callable(form):
  112              return form(val)
  113          if isinstance(form, tuple):
  114              func, args = form[0], form[1:]
  115              args = args + (val,)
  116              return func(*args)
  117      return reduce(evalform_back, forms, val)

  120  def instanceproperty(fget=None, fset=None, fdel=None, doc=None, classval=None):
  121      """ Like @property, but returns ``classval`` when used as a class attribute
  122  
  123      >>> class MyClass(object):
  124      ...     '''The class docstring'''
  125      ...     @instanceproperty(classval=__doc__)
  126      ...     def __doc__(self):
  127      ...         return 'An object docstring'
  128      ...     @instanceproperty
  129      ...     def val(self):
  130      ...         return 42
  131      ...
  132      >>> MyClass.__doc__
  133      'The class docstring'
  134      >>> MyClass.val is None
  135      True
  136      >>> obj = MyClass()
  137      >>> obj.__doc__
  138      'An object docstring'
  139      >>> obj.val
  140      42
  141      """
  142      if fget is None:
  143          return partial(instanceproperty, fset=fset, fdel=fdel, doc=doc,
  144                         classval=classval)
  145      return InstanceProperty(fget=fget, fset=fset, fdel=fdel, doc=doc,
  146                              classval=classval)

  149  class InstanceProperty(property):
  150      """ Like @property, but returns ``classval`` when used as a class attribute
  151  
  152      Should not be used directly.  Use ``instanceproperty`` instead.
  153      """
  154      def __init__(self, fget=None, fset=None, fdel=None, doc=None,
  155                   classval=None):
  156          self.classval = classval
  157          property.__init__(self, fget=fget, fset=fset, fdel=fdel, doc=doc)
  158  
  159      def __get__(self, obj, type=None):
  160          if obj is None:
  161              return self.classval
  162          return property.__get__(self, obj, type)
  163  
  164      def __reduce__(self):
  165          state = (self.fget, self.fset, self.fdel, self.__doc__, self.classval)
  166          return InstanceProperty, state
